svg.text: HOW CRUCIBLE WORKS
Every box is a step that runs.
YOU PROVIDE
A table, and one sentence
Your CSV or Parquet file, and the column you are trying to predict.
Then the sentence nothing else can supply: when the prediction happens in real life.
Optionally your data dictionary, which turns every verdict into a documented one.
FIRST, A CHECK
Do the column names actually mean anything?
V1, V2, V3 cannot be read
yes
SCREEN ONE
What the names mean
A language model is asked, for every column at once: could
this value have been known at your prediction point?
The columns are shuffled and the question asked again, once
or three times depending on how much that model's answers
move when the order changes.
An answer covering less than 90% of the table, or naming
columns the table does not have, is thrown away and asked
again. A majority of the passes settles each column.
SCREEN TWO
What the numbers say
The plain statistical check, on the same columns: how
strongly does each one correlate with the target?
Anything above 0.5 is flagged.
This one is here to be disagreed with. The two screens fail
in opposite directions, and the columns they disagree about
are the interesting ones: a leak with no correlation, or a
strong honest predictor that a threshold would delete.
SORTED
Which screens flagged it
both screens
obvious
the model only
the interesting group
statistics only
usually a strong honest column
neither
left alone
no
the reading
step is
skipped, and
the report
says so
IF YOU BROUGHT DOCUMENTATION
The column gets to defend itself
Every flagged column is checked back against your own data dictionary. If the documentation
says the value was already fixed at the moment you predict, the column is marked contested
and the decision is handed to you rather than made for you.
YOU DECIDE
Nothing is deleted for you
You confirm or reject each flagged column, with the reason and the evidence in front of you.
On the smallest dataset we tested, every model dropped one column too many, and that cost
more accuracy than the leak did. This step is a person, not a setting.
optional, and it takes a few minutes
MEASURE THE DAMAGE
Rebuild the model with and without
Three versions are fitted: every column, your confirmed drops removed, and, to keep everyone
honest, what a correlation threshold would have removed instead.
Two model families, three settings each, five folds. Ninety fits in all.
Every version gets identical folds, identical encoding and an identical search, so the clean one
is the best version of itself and not a strawman. The decision threshold is chosen inside the
training folds only, never on the rows being scored.
YOU GET
the cleaned file
your table without the columns you confirmed
the report
every column, verdict and reason, as JSON
the figures
vector, ready to drop into a paper
The reading step agrees with a source-grounded answer key 0.90 of the time across 12 datasets.
The correlation check, handed its best possible cutoff in hindsight, reaches 0.63.
